title: OSHA general industry occupational noise exposure practice questions
description: Free OSHA noise practice questions on 29 CFR 1910.95: Table G-16, the 85 dB action level, audiograms and hearing protectors, each linked to its source.

questions.question: Under Table G-16 in 29 CFR 1910.95, what is the longest permissible duration per day at a sound level of 95 dBA, slow response?
questions.explanation: In Table G-16, a "Duration per day, hours" of 4 is paired with 95 under "Sound level dBA slow response." Longer durations are paired with lower levels: 8 hours with 90 dBA and 6 hours with 92 dBA.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.95, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Duration per day, hours Sound level dBA slow response 8 90 6 92 4 95 3 97 2 100

questions.question: Employees are subjected to sound exceeding the levels in Table G-16. What does 1910.95(b)(1) require the employer to use?

options.A: Warning signs posted at the work area
options.B: A written notice to the OSHA area office
options.D: A medical examination of each exposed employee

questions.explanation: When employees are subjected to sound exceeding Table G-16, "feasible administrative or engineering controls shall be utilized." If they fail to reduce sound levels within the table, personal protective equipment must be provided and used.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.95, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: When employees are subjected to sound exceeding those listed in Table G-16, feasible administrative or engineering controls shall be utilized.

questions.question: Under 1910.95, exposure to impulsive or impact noise should not exceed what level?
questions.explanation: "Exposure to impulsive or impact noise should not exceed 140 dB peak sound pressure level."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.95, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Exposure to impulsive or impact noise should not exceed 140 dB peak sound pressure level.

questions.question: Under 1910.95(c)(1), what is the lowest exposure at which the employer must administer a hearing conservation program?

options.A: An 8-hour TWA of 90 decibels or a dose of 100 percent
options.D: An 8-hour TWA of 85 decibels or a dose of fifty percent

questions.explanation: The program is required "whenever employee noise exposures equal or exceed an 8-hour time-weighted average sound level (TWA) of 85 decibels measured on the A scale (slow response) or, equivalently, a dose of fifty percent." The higher levels listed are also covered, but 85 decibels is where the requirement starts.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.95, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: whenever employee noise exposures equal or exceed an 8-hour time-weighted average sound level (TWA) of 85 decibels measured on the A scale (slow response) or, equivalently, a dose of fifty percent.

questions.question: When employee noise exposures are computed for the hearing conservation program, how is the attenuation of hearing protectors treated?

options.A: The full NRR is subtracted from the measured level
options.B: It is not counted: exposures are computed without regard to it
options.C: Half of the NRR is subtracted from the measured level
options.D: 7 dB is subtracted from the measured level

questions.explanation: For the hearing conservation program, exposures are computed under Appendix A and Table G-16a "without regard to any attenuation provided by the use of personal protective equipment."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.95, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: employee noise exposures shall be computed in accordance with appendix A and Table G-16a, and without regard to any attenuation provided by the use of personal protective equipment.

questions.question: Paragraphs (c) through (n) of 1910.95 do not apply to employers engaged in which operations?

options.A: Oil and gas well drilling and servicing operations

questions.explanation: Paragraphs (c) through (n) "shall not apply to employers engaged in oil and gas well drilling and servicing operations."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.95, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Paragraphs (c) through (n) of this section shall not apply to employers engaged in oil and gas well drilling and servicing operations.

questions.question: Under 1910.95(d)(2), which range of sound levels must be integrated into the noise measurements?
questions.explanation: "All continuous, intermittent and impulsive sound levels from 80 decibels to 130 decibels shall be integrated into the noise measurements."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.95, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: All continuous, intermittent and impulsive sound levels from 80 decibels to 130 decibels shall be integrated into the noise measurements.

questions.question: High worker mobility makes area monitoring generally inappropriate at a plant. What must the employer use for monitoring, unless it can show area sampling produces equivalent results?

options.A: A single area reading taken once a year
options.B: Readings taken only at the loudest machine
options.D: Employee answers to a noise questionnaire

questions.explanation: Where high worker mobility, significant variations in sound level, or a significant component of impulse noise make area monitoring generally inappropriate, the employer "shall use representative personal sampling" unless it can show that area sampling produces equivalent results.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.95, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Where circumstances such as high worker mobility, significant variations in sound level, or a significant component of impulse noise make area monitoring generally inappropriate, the employer shall use representative personal sampling to comply with the monitoring requirements of this paragraph unless the employer can show that area sampling produces equivalent results.

questions.question: Which appendix to 1910.95 is labeled non-mandatory?

options.B: Appendix B, Methods for Estimating the Adequacy of Hearing Protector Attenuation
options.C: Appendix F, Calculations and Application of Age Corrections to Audiograms

questions.explanation: Appendix F's heading says "This appendix Is Non-Mandatory." Paragraph (n)(1) states that Appendices A, B, C, D and E "are mandatory."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.95, Appendix F (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Appendix F to § 1910.95-Calculations and Application of Age Corrections to Audiograms This appendix Is Non-Mandatory

questions.question: No mobile test van is used. Within what time of an employee's first exposure at or above the action level must the employer establish a valid baseline audiogram?
questions.explanation: "Within 6 months of an employee's first exposure at or above the action level, the employer shall establish a valid baseline audiogram." The 1-year limit applies only where mobile test vans are used.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.95, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Within 6 months of an employee's first exposure at or above the action level, the employer shall establish a valid baseline audiogram against which subsequent audiograms can be compared.

questions.question: Where mobile test vans are used to meet the audiometric testing obligation, the valid baseline audiogram must be obtained within what time of first exposure at or above the action level?
questions.explanation: Under the mobile test van exception, the employer "shall obtain a valid baseline audiogram within 1 year of an employee's first exposure at or above the action level."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.95, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Where mobile test vans are used to meet the audiometric testing obligation, the employer shall obtain a valid baseline audiogram within 1 year of an employee's first exposure at or above the action level.

questions.question: Testing to establish a baseline audiogram must be preceded by at least how many hours without exposure to workplace noise?
questions.explanation: Baseline testing "shall be preceded by at least 14 hours without exposure to workplace noise." Hearing protectors may be used as a substitute for that requirement.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.95, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Testing to establish a baseline audiogram shall be preceded by at least 14 hours without exposure to workplace noise.

questions.question: What does 1910.95(g)(2) say about what the audiometric testing program costs employees?

options.A: It is provided at no cost to employees
options.B: Employees pay half of each test
options.C: Employees pay for annual audiograms only
options.D: Employees pay for the baseline audiogram only

questions.explanation: "The program shall be provided at no cost to employees."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.95, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The program shall be provided at no cost to employees.

questions.question: How does 1910.95(g)(10) define a standard threshold shift?

options.A: A change of 20 dB or more at 500 Hz in both ears
options.B: An average change of 5 dB or more at 1000, 2000 and 3000 Hz in both ears
options.C: A change of 15 dB or more at 6000 Hz in either ear
options.D: An average change of 10 dB or more at 2000, 3000 and 4000 Hz in either ear

questions.explanation: A standard threshold shift is "a change in hearing threshold relative to the baseline audiogram of an average of 10 dB or more at 2000, 3000, and 4000 Hz in either ear."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.95, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: a standard threshold shift is a change in hearing threshold relative to the baseline audiogram of an average of 10 dB or more at 2000, 3000, and 4000 Hz in either ear.

questions.question: An annual audiogram compared to the baseline shows a standard threshold shift has occurred. Within how many days of the determination must the employee be informed in writing?
questions.explanation: If a standard threshold shift has occurred, "the employee shall be informed of this fact in writing, within 21 days of the determination."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.95, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: the employee shall be informed of this fact in writing, within 21 days of the determination.

questions.question: An employee who does not use hearing protectors has a standard threshold shift, and no physician has found it is not work related. What must the employer ensure?

options.A: The employee is moved out of the noisy job permanently
options.B: The employee receives a written warning
options.C: The employee is fitted with hearing protectors, trained in their use and care, and required to use them
options.D: The employee is retested every month until hearing returns

questions.explanation: Unless a physician determines the shift is not work related or aggravated by occupational noise, "Employees not using hearing protectors shall be fitted with hearing protectors, trained in their use and care, and required to use them."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.95, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Employees not using hearing protectors shall be fitted with hearing protectors, trained in their use and care, and required to use them.

questions.question: An employee exposed to an 8-hour TWA of 87 decibels has experienced a standard threshold shift. What does 1910.95(i)(2) require?

options.A: Hearing protectors are optional for this employee
options.B: Hearing protectors are required only above an 8-hour TWA of 90 decibels
options.C: Hearing protectors are required only if the employee asks for them
options.D: The employer must ensure hearing protectors are worn

questions.explanation: Employers must ensure hearing protectors are worn by any employee "exposed to an 8-hour time-weighted average of 85 decibels or greater" who has experienced a standard threshold shift.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.95, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: By any employee who is exposed to an 8-hour time-weighted average of 85 decibels or greater, and who: (A) Has not yet had a baseline audiogram established pursuant to paragraph (g)(5)(ii); or (B) Has experienced a standard threshold shift.

questions.question: For employees who have experienced a standard threshold shift, hearing protectors must attenuate exposure to what 8-hour TWA?
questions.explanation: "For employees who have experienced a standard threshold shift, hearing protectors must attenuate employee exposure to an 8-hour time-weighted average of 85 decibels or below." For other employees, paragraph (j)(2) requires attenuation "at least to an 8-hour time-weighted average of 90 decibels."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.95, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: For employees who have experienced a standard threshold shift, hearing protectors must attenuate employee exposure to an 8-hour time-weighted average of 85 decibels or below.

questions.question: How often must the hearing conservation training program be repeated for each employee included in the program?
questions.explanation: "The training program shall be repeated annually for each employee included in the hearing conservation program."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.95, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The training program shall be repeated annually for each employee included in the hearing conservation program.

questions.question: Under 1910.95(m)(3), for at least how long must noise exposure measurement records be retained?
questions.explanation: "Noise exposure measurement records shall be retained for two years." Audiometric test records are kept for the duration of the affected employee's employment.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.95, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Noise exposure measurement records shall be retained for two years.
